title: Applying the Vertical Line Test to First-Quadrant Curves
originalTopic: Functions and Graphs: Vertical Line Test
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Consider two curves in the first quadrant: (a) a curve that starts on the positive y-axis, bends to reach a leftmost tangent point on the y-axis, and curves back to the right toward the positive x-axis; (b) a wave-like curve that progresses strictly from left to right with a single peak and valley. Determine which graph represents a function of x and justify your answer.
finalAnswer: \text{(a) Not a function of } x; \quad \text{(b) Function of } x

steps.title: State the Vertical Line Test Criterion
steps.mathExpression: x = c \text{ intersects the graph at most once}
steps.explanation: By definition, a curve in the xy-plane is the graph of a function of x if and only if no vertical line x = c intersects the curve more than once.
steps.why: A function assigns to each input x in its domain at most one output value y = f(x).

steps.title: Test Graph (a) with Vertical Lines
steps.mathExpression: x = c > 0 \implies \text{two intersection points } (c, y_1) \text{ and } (c, y_2)
steps.explanation: In graph (a), because the curve doubles back horizontally in the first quadrant, vertical lines x = c for positive values of c pass through both an upper branch and a lower branch of the curve.
steps.why: Multiple y-values for a single x-value violate the uniqueness requirement of a function.

steps.title: Test Graph (b) with Vertical Lines
steps.explanation: In graph (b), as x increases from left to right, the curve never folds back over itself; every vertical line intersects the curve at most once.
steps.why: Each x-coordinate in the domain corresponds to a unique y-coordinate on the curve.

steps.title: Formulate the Final Conclusion
steps.mathExpression: \text{(a) Not a function of } x; \quad \text{(b) Function of } x
steps.explanation: Graph (a) fails the Vertical Line Test and is not the graph of a function of x, whereas graph (b) passes the Vertical Line Test and defines y as a function of x.
steps.why: The Vertical Line Test is a necessary and sufficient geometric condition for a plane curve to represent a function y = f(x).
